events.title: Development of environmentalism as part of popular culture
events.description: A multi‑decadal process in which environmentalism became integrated into mainstream Western popular culture, characterized by countercultural roots, the rise of consumerism, media influence, and celebrity involvement over roughly the past sixty years.
events.supporting_text: This chapter has examined how environmentalism developed as part of popular culture over the past sixty years. In the 1960s, environmental issues burst into the public consciousness with unprecedented speed and urgency. During these early years, environmentalism had a clear countercultural element, and this has stayed with it over half a century of campaigns, protests and boycotts. The rise of consumerism, influence of the media and emergence of celebrity have all contributed to making environmentalism part of western mainstream culture.

significance.justification: Shows how environmentalism has become embedded in culture, indicating a systemic shift toward broader societal engagement with nature.

significance.justification: The survey reveals public confusion and misperceptions about green lifestyles, diagnosing a barrier to harmony with nature.
